parsed.why: Strong state protections: broad nondiscrimination since 2006, gender-identity hate-crime law, 2023 shield law, gender-neutral restrooms and city self-ID bathroom access. National border/passport exposure persists, capping the score in Elevated Risk.

Most protective dossier: GENDA, 2024 constitutional amendment, hate-crime and panic-defence repeal, X markers, mandated gender-neutral restrooms, shield law and repealed loitering statute. National entry/document exposure still limits it below Reduced Risk.

Worst-law grouping: school and college bathroom bans, binary-sex statute, no statewide nondiscrimination or gender-identity hate-crime coverage, low support. Surgery-requirement ID rules and hostile facilities exposure dominate; visitor has no state recourse.

Stripped gender-identity protections from civil-rights law, barred stronger local ordinances, and imposes birth-certificate bathroom rule on all school grounds including visitors. No documented general adult facility ban, but no state remedy if refused service.

Statewide nondiscrimination since 2008, gender-identity hate-crime penalties, panic-defence abolition, accessible X markers and 2023 shield law. Lacks documented restroom-access protection; national border and document exposure remains the limiting factor.
